Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation expectations

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call: 

Recap:
- Primary concern: strict data isolation for production ML workloads (customer PII and transaction data).
- Evaluating two deployment modes: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) vs Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem).
- Key questions: tenant isolation guarantees, network egress controls, key management (KMS/HSM), audit logs, and whether any customer data leaves their VPC.

What I heard as requirements:
1) No co-tenancy at the data plane (you want to ensure customer data is not shared with other tenants).
2) Data residency within your cloud account/VPC or fully on-prem (depending on the option).
3) Keys must be managed by your KMS or HSM; we should support customer-managed keys.
4) Full audit logs and the ability to export logs to your SIEM.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short comparison doc (redwood-dedicated-vs-private-vpc-comparison.pdf) and a QA checklist (FinSecure_Roadmap_QA_checklist.pdf) that maps our features to the items you raised.

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll loop in Marissa (solutions architecture) and Neha (security) to validate the technical controls.
- Can we schedule a 45-minute technical follow-up next week to walk through network diagrams and KMS options? Suggested window: Tue 28 Jul, 10:00 AM PT.
- If you can confirm whether you require on-prem (air-gapped) vs VPC-only, we’ll prepare the right architecture options.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with an invite once I get confirmation on timing.

Thanks Mateo — good recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our baseline requirement is that production model inference of customer data must not be processed on shared instances with other customers. In practice that means either dedicated GPU pools with guaranteed single-tenant assignment OR a Private VPC/on-prem deployment.
- We need data plane network isolation: the inference service must sit in our VPC (or in our on-prem environment) and be reachable only over our private network. No unexpected egress to third-party network segments.
- Keys: we require customer-managed KMS/HSM for encryption-at-rest and in-use protection for model artifacts and any cached data.
- Auditability: we need full request/response audit logging (token redaction is okay) and the ability to ship logs to our Splunk instance.

Also worth flagging: procurement will prefer a hosted Dedicated option if it can meet the isolation and KMS requirements since it's faster to deploy than full on-prem. But we need to know the exact controls you can provide and the ramp timeline.

Can Marissa/Neha share a sample network diagram and a short checklist of what Dedicated vs Private would look like from a compliance standpoint?

—Alice

Alice — great summary, thanks. Short answers and a proposed plan: 

1) Dedicated vs Private (short):
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved GPU pools with tenant-level isolation at the runtime layer. GPUs and inference processes are reserved to your account; control plane remains hosted by Redwood. Network isolation for the data plane can be achieved via private peering and strong egress controls, but the control plane is still on Redwood-managed infrastructure. This is usually faster to roll out (2–6 weeks) and supports customer-managed KMS in many configurations.
- Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem): customer-managed VPC or on-prem deployment where both control and data planes are under your network/jurisdiction. No shared tenancy and full control over network topology and key management. This is preferred where procurement/compliance requires zero managed-control-plane exposure, but it takes longer to deploy (4–12+ weeks depending on on-prem).

2) KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can integrate with customer HSMs for key sealing.

3) Audit logs + SIEM: we can stream audit logs to your Splunk instance (S3 log export + Kinesis/HTTP ingestion depending on your architecture). Logs can be token-redacted at ingestion.

4) Next steps (technical follow-up):
- Proposed: 45-minute call Tue Jul 28 at 10:00 AM PT with Marissa (solutions architect) and Neha (security).
- Action items for FinSecure: share a sample network diagram and confirm whether on-prem is required or VPC-only is acceptable.
- Action items for Redwood: Marissa will prepare a short comparison diagram and Neha will assemble a controls checklist mapping to your SOC2 / KMS / logging asks.

I’ll send a calendar invite now. If that time doesn’t work, send a few alternatives.
